main_topics.reason: The user came wanting to understand the POTS diagnosis and asked follow-up questions about what it means.
The user asked what they could do, sought practical steps to write down, and asked how to manage racing-heart episodes.
The user described a pounding heart, dizziness, lightheadedness, and spotty vision when standing.
The user explicitly asked whether POTS meant their heart was damaged and said that possibility scared them.
The user asked why POTS followed long COVID and connected it to a major change from their previous health and activity.
The user asked whether POTS would be permanent or whether people get better.
The user said exertion with long COVID causes crashes lasting days and that this made exercise advice frightening.
The user asked whether they should be on medication because their doctor had not prescribed any.
The user said the diagnosis was explained too quickly at the appointment and later found the conversation more useful than what they received there.

output.summary: The user sought an explanation of POTS diagnosed after long COVID, asking about standing symptoms, heart damage, prognosis, and management. The assistant explained self-management options and addressed the user's concern that exercise triggers days-long crashes; the user said they felt less panicked, understood that their heart was not broken, and had written down practical steps.
